Kadence Security plugin for WordPress (better-wp-security) before 10.0.6.1 contains a brute-force protection bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to evade per-host login lockouts by exploiting IPv6 address handling in ITSEC_Lib::get_ip(), which keys failed-login counters on the full 128-bit IPv6 address rather than a /64 prefix. Attackers who control a routed IPv6 /64 can send each login attempt from a new address within that prefix, resetting the per-host counter each time

Attackers controlling a routable IPv6 /64 prefix can send each login attempt from a fresh address within that range, preventing any counter from reaching the lockout threshold and enabling effectively unlimited brute-for

Bonsai through 6.0 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated Editor users to access admin pages because AdminAuthHandler accepts both Administrator and Editor roles. Attackers can use UsersController and DynamicConfigController to reset administrator passwords, promote accounts to Administrator, and change global settings to take over the instance.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: x86: Unconditionally reset MMU context when emulating INIT

Force an MMU reset when emulating an INIT even if paging was already
disabled, as the MMU page role includes guest_mode (L2), i.e. an INIT while
L2 is running with CR0.PG=0 will result in KVM running L1 with a stale MMU
context.

Alternatively, the reset could be scoped strictly to paging being enabled
or L2 being active, but SMM is also encoded in the page role.

The core JDK HTTP client (a2a-java-sdk-http-client) applies the GHSA-9rhm redirect-neutralization only to the POST path. JdkGetBuilder.get(), JdkGetBuilder.getAsyncSSE(), and JdkDeleteBuilder.delete() call the injected httpClient directly, with no redirect gate. An application that supplies a redirect-capable HttpClient (Redirect.NORMAL/ALWAYS) — which is the SDK-documented way to enable POST redirects — silently follows cross-authority redirects on every credentialed GET/DELETE request. The JDK

The Vert.x HTTP client transport (a2a-java-sdk-http-client-vertx) hand-rolls a POST redirect follower that, when the documented PostBuilder.followRedirects(true) opt-in is enabled, re-issues the redirected request with the full request header map copied verbatim and performs no credential stripping and no same-authority check. Radicale 3.3.0 before 3.8.3 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inherit group-based rights by reusing group memberships never reset between requests. Attackers can send credential-less requests after a group member logs in to read and write group-shared calendar and address book collections evaluated by the from_file rights backend.

Our WordPress plugin for the pretix Widget performs HTTP calls to pre-fetch CSS and JS files into a local cache and stores them publicly on the WordPress instance. These HTTP calls are made with wp_remote_get, not wp_safe_remote_get, and therefore allow SSRF with body extraction. Exploiting this requires sufficient WordPress permissions to create or modify pages.

The Envira Gallery  WordPress plugin before 1.16.4 does not apply its own gallery-permission policy until an administrator first opens its permissions screen, instead copying gallery-management capabilities onto each role from that role's core post capabilities after activation, which lets Contributor accounts create, edit and delete galleries that the policy is meant to restrict to higher roles.

The Royal Addons for Elementor  WordPress plugin before 1.7.1071 does not restrict or validate the post meta keys used when counting or rendering a filtered grid, and does not reject private (hidden) meta keys, allowing unauthenticated users to disclose the value of arbitrary private post meta one value at a time from the filtered result count. This is an incomplete fix of CVE-2026-17585, whose 1.7.1067 patch covered only a separate search-based path and left the grid filtering path affected.

The Search & Replace WordPress plugin before 3.2.4 does not correctly restrict which database tables an administrator of a single site may operate on in a multisite network, allowing subsite administrators to read and modify the tables of other sites and of the network, and to make themselves Super Admin.

The Search & Replace WordPress plugin before 3.2.4 does not restrict one of its database tools to network administrators on multisite installations, allowing administrators of a single subsite to run arbitrary SQL against the whole network's database and make themselves Super Admin.

The Flatsome WordPress theme before 3.20.13 does not perform a capability or nonce check on an AJAX action available to authenticated users, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to disclose the name and content of non-public templates stored on the site.

The Flatsome WordPress theme before 3.20.13 does not verify that the acting user is authorised to modify the target post when saving a template, allowing users with a role as low as Contributor to overwrite the content and type of an arbitrary post, including another user's published page, removing it from the front end.

The Flatsome WordPress theme before 3.20.13 does not sanitise post meta saved through an AJAX action, nor escape it when rendering the product page, allowing users with a role as low as Contributor (who lack the unfiltered_html capability) to store JavaScript that executes in the browser of anyone who views the product, including administrators.

The Dynific Addons for Elementor (formerly Anywhere Elementor) WordPress plugin before 1.3.1 does not perform a capability check on an AJAX action that stores a configuration value, allowing any authenticated user, including Subscribers, to store a value that is later output without proper escaping in a quoted attribute on an administrator settings page, resulting in Stored Cross-Site Scripting that executes in the administrator's session.

The WPvivid — Backup, Migration & Staging WordPress plugin before 0.9.140 does not limit its table prefix rewrite to table names when restoring a database backup, which corrupts the length of stored serialized values and allows users with a role as low as Subscriber to plant a PHP object that WordPress instantiates after an administrator restores a backup.

The WPvivid — Backup, Migration & Staging WordPress plugin before 0.9.140 does not prevent serialized data it cannot safely unserialize from being re-serialized as a PHP object during a site migration, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to plant a PHP object that WordPress instantiates after an administrator restores a backup onto a different URL.

The Contact Form 7 WordPress plugin before 6.2.5 does not check that the post a form submission says it was sent from is publicly viewable before resolving post-related mail-tags, allowing unauthenticated users to obtain the title, URL, author name and author email of private, draft and trashed posts where such tags are used in an email or message returned to the submitter.

The Otter Blocks  WordPress plugin before 3.2.10 does not use URL-aware escaping when it resolves its dynamic data tags inside HTML attributes, which could allow unauthenticated users to post comments containing links that execute arbitrary JavaScript when clicked, for example by a logged-in administrator.

The Hide My WP Ghost  WordPress plugin before 7.0.19 does not remove or restrict a debug branch in its output rewriting, allowing unauthenticated attackers to reveal the hidden login page, the hidden admin path and the renamed content folders the Hide My WP Ghost  WordPress plugin before 7.0.19 is meant to conceal.

The RSVP and Event Management WordPress plugin before 2.7.19 does not sanitise and escape attendee data imported from a spreadsheet before outputting it on the frontend RSVP form, which could allow users with the Author role and above to perform Stored Cross-Site Scripting attacks against anyone, including administrators, viewing the affected attendee, even when the unfiltered_html capability is disallowed.

The Probono Form Basic WordPress plugin before 1.3.3 does not validate the real type of files uploaded through its public form, trusting the client-declared MIME type instead, which could allow unauthenticated attackers to upload PHP files to a public directory and execute them before they are deleted, on servers that do not honour the Probono Form Basic WordPress plugin before 1.3.3's Apache-only access restriction.

The OneLogin SAML SSO WordPress plugin before 3.7.1 does not validate a user-supplied parameter before using it to redirect an already-authenticated user, allowing unauthenticated attackers to redirect a logged-in user to an arbitrary external domain via a crafted link (e.g. for phishing).

The Edwiser Bridge  WordPress plugin before 4.3.5 does not correctly scope one of its REST API authentication checks, disabling WordPress's REST nonce validation for every route on the site, which allows attackers to make a logged-in administrator perform arbitrary privileged actions, such as creating a new administrator account, via CSRF.

The Team Members WordPress plugin before 5.4.2 does not properly escape a team member field when it is rendered back in the administration area, allowing users with the contributor role and above to perform Stored Cross-Site Scripting attacks against higher-privileged users who edit the team.

The Team Members WordPress plugin before 5.4.2 does not properly escape team member social link URLs when they are rendered back in the administration area, allowing users with the Contributor role and above to perform Stored Cross-Site Scripting attacks against higher privileged users who edit the team.

In Eclipse Mosquitto versions 2.0.0 to 2.0.22 and 2.1.0 to 2.1.2, the return value of password hash functions for sha512-pbkdf2 and legacy sha512 were not checked. Starting with OpenSSL 4.0, sha512-pbkdf2 hashing will fail when using the FIPS provider for passwords shorter than 8 characters. This has the effect that newly created passwords would match against any other password with fewer than 8 characters.
